summary.text: Susan Humphries is a Republican state representative who has represented Kansas House of Representatives District 99 since 2017 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
An attorney who practiced adoption law, she chairs the House Judiciary Committee and the Rules and Journal Committee.

paragraphs.text: Susan Humphries lives in Wichita, Kansas, and earned a BFA in communications from Texas Christian University and a law degree from the University of Denver in 2014.
Her career experience includes working in advertising and marketing, as a caseworker with Big Brothers Big Sisters, and as an adoption attorney.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she is the coordinator of Wichita Christian Legal Aid.
Humphries took office in the Kansas House on January 9, 2017.

For 2025-2026, she was assigned to the House Judiciary Committee as chair and the Rules and Journal Committee as chair, and she also served on the Child Welfare and Foster Care, Welfare Reform, Child Welfare System Oversight, and State-Tribal Relations committees and as vice chair of the Special Claims Against the State Committee.
She faces Democrat Mark Barlow in the general election.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a traditional conservative advocating for small accountable government, constitutional liberties, protection of life from conception to natural death, and educational choice.
